Package com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog

Class PumpButtonHistoryLog

java.lang.Object
com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog.HistoryLog
com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog.PumpButtonHistoryLog
public class PumpButtonHistoryLog extends HistoryLog
A press or release of the pump's button, with a millisecond timestamp. Seen on the t:slim X2 and the Tandem Mobi.

Tandem's export and its Mobi app do not name this opcode, so the class name and the button interpretation are provisional. The layout is well supported: uint32 timeOfDayMs at bytes 10-13, state at byte 14, zeros at 15-25 (1772/1772 records from at least 8 pumps, X2 and Mobi).

The button reading rests on three observations. On the Mobi, where tubing is filled by holding the pump button, every tubing-prime start (PrimeInprocessHistoryLog) was immediately preceded by one of these with state 1 (113/113 on 4 pumps). A triple press (1, 0, 1, 0, 1 within 0.6 s) was immediately followed by a SnoozeActivatedHistoryLog in the same second. On the X2, whose button wakes the screen, press/release pairs typically last about 0.2 s. See https://github.com/jwoglom/pumpx2/issues/148.

    • getTimeOfDayMs

      public long getTimeOfDayMs()
      Milliseconds since midnight on the pump's local clock, the same clock as HistoryLog.getPumpTimeSec(): timeOfDayMs / 1000 == pumpTimeSec % 86400 in 1772/1772 records. It gives sub-second ordering within the record's second; it is not a motor or encoder count.

    • getState

      public int getState()
      Byte 14: 1 or 0, alternating (880 records with 1, 892 with 0). Read as 1 = pressed, 0 = released; see the class comment for why that reading is provisional.
